40 Which particle is a hadron?
A
electron
B
neutrino
C
positron
D
proton

hints: Notice the question asks for a hadron, which means a particle that is made of quarks, not a fundamental lepton.
Recall that electrons, neutrinos and their antiparticles belong to the lepton family and do not experience the strong force.
Check which of the four listed particles has an internal quark structure of the form $uud$ and is classed as a baryon.
walkthrough: Identify the test: a hadron is any particle made of quarks, divided into baryons made of three quarks and mesons made of a quark-antiquark pair.
Recall the lepton family: the electron, neutrino and positron are all leptons or antileptons and are fundamental particles with no quark structure.
Consider the proton: it is not fundamental and has quark composition $uud$, so it is a three-quark baryon.
Since baryons are one type of hadron, the proton satisfies the definition while the other three particles do not.

A.explanation: The electron is a lepton and is fundamental, so it is not made of quarks and is not a hadron.

B.explanation: The neutrino is a lepton and is fundamental, so it is not made of quarks and is not a hadron.

C.explanation: The positron is the antiparticle of the electron and is an antilepton, so it is not a hadron.

D.explanation: The proton is a baryon hadron made of three quarks with quark composition $uud$.
